name: FRED — Data health
description: Is the measurement itself working. READ THE CAVEAT: two of the three things worth watching cannot be answered from PostHog at all, by construction. An opted-out user sends NOTHING, so PostHog cannot know the opt-out share; a suppressed or parked outbox row is never sent, so PostHog cannot see it either. Those come from the MySQL views v_consent and v_outbox_reconciliation, and the tiles here are what PostHog genuinely can answer.

tiles.name: Events per day, by name
tiles.description: The first place a broken emitter shows up. A line that goes flat at zero is a wiring regression; a line that doubles overnight is usually a retry loop.

tiles.name: Server events per day
tiles.description: The money and compliance spine. These come through the outbox, so a gap here means the publisher stopped, not that users stopped: check pending_count in v_outbox_reconciliation.

tiles.name: Client events per day
tiles.description: Device-side events. Unlike the server ones these depend on a phone being awake and on consent, so a dip here can be real behaviour, a release problem, or more people opting out.

tiles.name: Consent changes
tiles.description: setting_changed where setting = analytics_consent. This is the nearest PostHog can get to an opt-out rate, and it is NOT one: a user who opts out stops sending, so their later behaviour is invisible and the opt-out itself is the last thing you see from them. v_consent in MySQL has the real share.
